title: Vishwanath & Sons Trailer: Suriya Plays Olympic Shooter in Venky Atluri's Emotional Bilingual Drama
excerpt: The three-minute trailer reveals Suriya as a pistol-shooting Olympian and single father navigating an age-gap romance in his second film after the massive success of Karuppu.
body:
• Suriya stars as Sanjay Vishwanath, an Olympic pistol shooter and single father whose son needs a bone marrow transplant in the Tamil-Telugu bilingual
  • The film also stars Mamitha Baiju as the 20-years-younger love interest, with Raveena Tandon returning to Tamil cinema after 25 years
  • Directed by Venky Atluri of Lucky Bhaskar fame, Vishwanath & Sons releases August 14, 2026, clashing with Awarapan 2 and Batwara 1947

The full trailer for Vishwanath & Sons dropped today, giving audiences a detailed look at Suriya's multi-layered role as Sanjay Vishwanath — an Olympic pistol shooter, wealthy businessman, and single father dealing with a family medical crisis and an unexpected romance. The Tamil-Telugu bilingual, directed by Venky Atluri, is set for a worldwide theatrical release on August 14, 2026.

What the Trailer Reveals

The nearly three-minute trailer opens with Sanjay Vishwanath's mother dreaming of an Olympic gold medal for her son in pistol shooting. Sanjay is established as a popular national athlete and a rich businessman from a privileged family, but his world centers on his toddler son, Abhay, who needs bone marrow surgery.

When no suitable donor is found locally, Sanjay's doctor directs him to San Francisco to meet a potential match — Maddy, played by Mamitha Baiju. She is introduced as a free-spirited, bubbly young woman whose life changes after she agrees to be the donor. As Maddy grows closer to Sanjay and his child, a romance develops, but Sanjay is acutely aware of the 20-year age gap between them and pushes back before emotions escalate.

"A story of dreams, emotions, and unexpected love unfolds. Presenting the world of Sanjay Vishwanath."

— Official trailer tagline

Suriya's Post-Karuppu Momentum

Vishwanath & Sons is Suriya's second release after Karuppu, which was a massive box office hit. The trailer suggests a deliberate shift in register — from Karuppu's intensity to a more emotionally grounded family drama. Suriya's character doles out motivational life lessons to the media in multiple scenes, and the trailer also features several action sequences, including one where he takes on members of a political party.

For Suriya, who has had an uneven box office track record in recent years despite a loyal fanbase, the one-two punch of Karuppu's success and Vishwanath & Sons' emotional scope positions this as a pivotal year in his career.

Raveena Tandon Returns to Tamil Cinema

Raveena Tandon plays a pivotal role in the film — reportedly the mother of Sanjay's child — marking her return to Tamil cinema 25 years after Aalavandhan (2001). The trailer keeps details of her character deliberately ambiguous, adding to the intrigue. The supporting cast includes Radhika Sarathkumar, Bhavani Sre, Sunil Reddy, and Karate Karthi.

Atluri's First Tamil-Only Directorial

This is director Venky Atluri's first Tamil-only directorial project. His previous film, Lucky Bhaskar with Dulquer Salmaan, earned both critical appreciation and commercial success. Atluri brings several of his Lucky Bhaskar crew along, including cinematographer Nimish Ravi, production designer Banglan, and composer G.V. Prakash Kumar.

The film is produced by Suryadevara Naga Vamsi and Sai Soujanya under Sithara Entertainments and Fortune Four Cinemas, presented by Srikara Studios. Netflix has secured the streaming rights.

A Crowded Independence Day Weekend

Vishwanath & Sons releases on August 14 alongside Bollywood titles Awarapan 2 and Batwara 1947, making for one of the most competitive Independence Day weekends in recent memory. The Independence Day holiday on Saturday gives all three films an extended opening window.

For diaspora audiences, the San Francisco storyline and Suriya's massive following among Tamil communities worldwide make this one of the more anticipated South Indian releases of the summer.
